newsitem.title: POLAND: Hungary hits all-time high, other east mkts soak.
newsitem.headline: Hungary hits all-time high, other east mkts soak.

text.p: The Budapest bourse hit an all-time high this week while investors fled the floods in Poland and the Czech Republic and stayed tuned to forecasts of more rain over the weekend.
The Slovak bourse fell, Croatian shares were mixed and Romanian indices gained.
The CESI index, which follows price movements in 72 Hungarian, Polish, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian shares, ended the week down 1.57 percent to 1,426.74 points.
BUDAPEST
A mild downward correction on Wednesday was the only blemish on a bullish week in Budapest as the BUX index finished at an all-time high of 7,444.27 points on Thursday.

Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe in London, said the Hungarian market merited the current investor focus as domestic interest-rate trends and international market sentiment favoured the bourse.

"In the context of a good, healthy equity environment Hungary deserves the attention it is getting," Monson said, adding that though Hungary had a recovering economy and very good corporate performance the bourse was no longer cheap.
Analysts said the Hungarian market had also benefited from recent macroeconomic difficulties and floods in Poland and the Czech Republic.
PRAGUE
The effects of recent flooding in the eastern Czech Republic continued to dampen buying on the Prague bourse but the market rose slightly on the week thanks mainly to a solid rise in SPT Telecom.
The PX50 index gained 2.5 points, or 0.5 percent, from last Friday to 505.0.

Broader losses were countered by SPT's 177-crown gain on Tuesday and another 15 crowns on Thursday to 3,615, despite reports the company would lose hundreds of millions of crowns due to lost service and damaged infrastructure in the flooding.

"The biggest problem seems that the infrastructure is disrupted and it will take some time to organise (transport) and this will cause problems for the big companies," said Jindrich Weiss, analyst at Zivnostenska Banka.
WARSAW
Polish shares fell 2.7 percent this week to 15,406.1 points and analysts said the market would be watching to what degree forecasts of more heavy rain in coming days would come true.
On Thursday Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz warned parliament that weather forecasts showed heavy rain overnight and might cause a new wave of floods in the south.

"Current gains are a reaction to recent falls but the mood is pretty jittery with forecasts of more rain, which could have an effect tomorrow (Friday)," said Janusz Oleksak, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Analysts said investors were also concerned on the degree to which Poland's planned 2.8-percent 1997 budget deficit might be affected by flood relief aid.
BRATISLAVA

The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) continued its listless trading this week and brokers expected the situation to last at least until the end of the summer. The official 16-share SAX index dropped 1.8 points, or 0.59 percent.
"The index is more or less stable at the moment, indicating that the market hit its floor," said Creditanstalt's Libor Briska.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were mixed with top shares trading on exceptionally high volumes throughout the week, but market participants saw stagnation for most prices in days ahead.
Traders said rises in heavy trade by Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva were due to the strong dollar.
Others said the central bourse's recent decision to suspend taxes on deals made between mid-July and mid-August could help market liquidity during a usually dead summer season.
BUCHAREST
Stocks on the second tier, where listing criteria are lighter, moved to centre-stage this week as investors bought cheaper small caps, traders said.
Falls, especially in heavyweights, are expected for the next few sessions.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares rose two percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index increased 29.3 points to 1,469.47.
Turnover rose to 1.7 billion tolars ($10.4 million) from 1.3 billion tolars.
Traders saw the index stabilising or rising over the summer on expected continued inflow of foreign capital.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 19.7 percent while financial consultancy Finmedia led decliners, falling 4.09 percent.
